answer:
HYPOTHESIS: The highest-growth phase of the 2000–1100 BCE period is the 15th–14th centuries BCE (1500–1300 BCE), with the single strongest century being 1500–1401 BCE (15th century BCE, ≈ +0.19%/yr mean growth of the 100-year-smoped landscape-openness score). After openness collapsed to its window minimum around 1500 BCE (smoothed openness ≈ 0.03 PCA units; 0.36 on the 0–100 scale), it rebounded at the fastest sustained rates of the entire period through 1400–1300 BCE, reaching its window maximum around 1300–1200 BCE (2.04 / 2.49 PCA). This growth phase is corroborated by the broadest contemporaneous rise in capital indicators (into 1400–1301 BCE: symbolic +0.79, social +0.74, economic +0.87, all-groups +0.68 σ), whereas pottery-form/decoration (cultural) indicators stayed flat and slightly negative throughout — a flagged disagreement — and the strongest single-symbolic (weapon/deposition) values and the latest economic uptick (Z_Hort 3.38 at 1100 BCE) fall slightly after/aside from the pollen-growth peak.

RANKED CENTURIES (primary metric: per-century mean of pollen_grate_100, time_series_data.csv, window CE −2000…−1100):
1. 1500–1401 BCE +0.00189/yr (~+0.19%/yr) — BEST
2. 1400–1301 BCE +0.00111/yr
3. 1700–1601 BCE +0.00086/yr
4. 1900–1801 BCE +0.00017/yr
5. 1300–1201 BCE −0.00017/yr (but highest openness LEVEL, 2.04)
6. 1800–1701 BCE −0.00024/yr
7. 2000–1901 BCE −0.00090/yr
8. 1200–1101 BCE −0.00104/yr
9. 1100–1001 BCE −0.00256/yr (partial bin, 1 year)
10. 1600–1501 BCE −0.00301/yr — WORST (collapse into the trough)
Best contiguous 2-century phase: 1500–1401 + 1400–1301 BCE (sum +0.0030); best contiguous 3-century phase: 1500–1300 BCE extending into 1300–1201 BCE (sum +0.0028).

VERIFICATION OF pollen_grate_100 SCALE (requested, reported not assumed): numerically reconstructed exactly as grate(t) = [smooth100(t) − smooth100(t−1)] / [smooth100(t−1) + 4.54648], i.e., the PER-YEAR fractional change of the 100-year-smoothed interpolated openness curve on a baseline-rescaled scale (offset = 4.54648 fitted; median |reconstruction error| = 5.3e-10, max 1.4e-8, corr = 1.00000000, n = 3600). It is NOT a per-100-year percentage change; per-century ranking therefore uses the century mean of this annual rate (~±0.5%/yr typical magnitude).

CROSS-CHECK 1 — pollen PCA file (SMOOTH_MEAN_100y, Belau+Woserin mean), chronological century means: 2.14 → 2.13 → 2.58 → 1.70 → 0.62 → 0.03 (trough, 1500–1401 BCE) → 1.40 → 2.49 (peak) → 1.64 → 1.46. Steepest growth INTO 1400–1301 BCE (+1.37 PCA units; the +5053% figure is a near-zero-denominator artifact; absolute increment ranking: 1400s +1.37 > 1300s +1.10 > 1800s +0.45). Spearman(grate_mean, PCA %change) = 0.15; vs absolute increment = 0.35 — moderate agreement; both sources agree on the trough at ~1500 BCE and the 1500→1300 BCE recovery.

CROSS-CHECK 2 — capital groups (z-score means per century): the strongest broad-based improvement occurs INTO 1400–1301 BCE (symbolic +0.79, social +0.74, economic +0.87, overall +0.68), reaching symbolic 2.13–2.15 and economic 0.86; symbolic peaks at 1300–1201 BCE (2.15), social peaks at 1200–1101 BCE (1.20), economic spikes again at 1100–1001 BCE (+1.09, driven by Depot/Hort z = 3.38). Spearman with grate_mean: symbolic −0.01, social +0.17, economic +0.06, cultural −0.31, all −0.09 — weak year-to-century associations, but the phase-level alignment (trough-and-rebound coinciding with the biggest capital jump) is clear.

EDGE-BIN SENSITIVITY (explicit): the 1100–1001 BCE bin contains only CE −1100; its mean grate is −0.00256 (partial) vs +0.00029 if the full 1100–1001 bin were used. The top-3 ranking is IDENTICAL under partial-bin, full-bin, and excluded-bin treatments, so the conclusion is insensitive to this edge.

KEY CAVEATS: the 1500–1401 BCE top rank reflects steep within-century recovery from a near-zero level (its century-mean level is still the window minimum), so "highest growth" (rate) and "highest openness" (level, 1300–1201 BCE) point to adjacent centuries; raw pollen observations in the window are sparse (48 points, heavily interpolated); and the cultural-indicator group does not participate in the growth phase.

payload.hypothesis: The highest-growth phase between 2000 and 1100 BCE is the 15th-14th centuries BCE (1500-1300 BCE), peaking in the 15th century BCE (1500-1401 BCE, ~+0.19%/yr growth of the 100-year-smoothed openness score). Landscape openness collapsed to its period minimum around 1500 BCE and then rebounded at the fastest rates of the entire window through 1400-1300 BCE, reaching maximum openness levels around 1300-1200 BCE. This pollen-based growth phase coincides with the broadest rise in capital indicators (symbolic weapons, social house/monument investment, and economic metals/depots all jump into 1400-1301 BCE), although pottery-related (cultural) indicators remain flat - a noted exception - and the latest economic uptick (depot hoards at 1100 BCE) postdates the pollen-growth peak.
payload.highest_growth_phase: 1500-1300 BCE (15th-14th centuries BCE); openness level peaks in 1300-1201 BCE
payload.pollen_grate_100_scale_verified: grate(t) = [smooth100(t)-smooth100(t-1)]/[smooth100(t-1)+4.54648]; per-year fractional change (median abs reconstruction error 5.3e-10, corr 1.0)
payload.edge_bin_sensitivity: 1100s BCE bin has 1 annual row; partial -0.00256 vs full-bin +0.00029; top-3 ranking unchanged under all treatments

cross_checks.pca_pollen_file: trough 1500-1401 BCE (0.03); steepest rebound into 1400-1301 BCE (+1.37 PCA units) and 1300-1201 BCE (+1.10); Spearman vs grate_mean 0.15 (pct) / 0.35 (absolute)
cross_checks.capital_groups: broadest rise INTO 1400-1301 BCE (symbolic +0.79, social +0.74, economic +0.87, all +0.68); cultural flat/negative throughout (disagreement)

payload.workflow: Loaded three CSVs (capital.csv with decimal=','); restricted to CE -2000..-1100 (calBP 3050-3950, present=1950); verified calBP=1950-CE in all files; numerically reverse-engineered pollen_grate_100 (exact reconstruction); binned annual data into BCE centuries aligned to CE multiples of 100; ranked centuries by mean grate; cross-checked with century-over-century change of SMOOTH_MEAN_100y (PCA file) and per-century changes of four capital z-groups (symbolic/social/cultural/economic); tested 1100 BCE edge-bin sensitivity under three bin treatments; outputs in work/century_summary.csv, work/pca_century_summary.csv, work/capital_group_summary.csv.
